MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, May 3, 2021

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live streamed on the City' s website.
2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 31 p. m.
3.  Council Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robert Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Hepburn.

7.  2021- 22 Paramedic  Service  Interim Finance Director Alvarado reported on the 2021- 22 Paramedic Service
  Fee  Fee. He stated that the City's voter approved Paramedic Service Fee requires
  an annual hearing in order to consider a rate change. The monthly fee is
  subject to an annual adjustment for a rate change based on the Consumer
  Price Index

  Mayor Hepburn opened the public hearing and called for public comment.

  There was none.

  It was moyed by Davis, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried by roll
  call to adjust the monthly paramedic service fee from$ 5. 54 to$ 5. 58 by
  adopting Resolution No. 21- 22.

  Resolution  No. 21- 22,  Resolution No. 21- 22- A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE

  2021- 22
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 3, 2021, Page 3

  Continued  to the May 17, 2021  City Manager Russi and Assistant Planner Rivera reported on the proposed
  Short-Term Rental Ordinance. The City Council held a Short-Term Rental
  Proposed Short- Term Rental  (  STR) Study Session on December 20, 2020, to discuss the draft ordinance. In
  Ordinance  January of 2020, the City Council adopted a moratorium on short- term rentals
  less than 30 days) based on concerns raised at various locations within the
  City. After several extensions, the moratorium is set to expire on August 17,
  2021.  Staff has drafted an ordinance to regulate short- term rentals based on
  the input that City Council and the Planning Commission provided. Staff and
  the Planning Commission recommend that the City Council adopt Ordinance
  No. 1098, approving new regulations for short-term rentals

  City Attorney Kress reported that the Ordinance presented to the Council was
  the previous draft copy and that it still needed minor changes, like the effective
  date.

  The City Council agreed that they would like to see the final corrected version
  of the Ordinance before voting on the matter and agreed to continue the
  matter.

  Mayor Hepburn opened and closed the public hearing and continued the
  matter for decision to the May 17, 2021, Council Meeting so the final
  Ordinance can be presented.

  One phone communication  was received.

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  One email was received and is attached.

8.  Temporary Employment  Assistant to the City Manager Rannell reported on the Temporary Employment
  Agreement  Agreement  for Interim Fire Chief.  He stated that Interim Fire Chief David
  Segura notified the City he would be leaving his position effective as soon as
  possible. After conducting a search of qualifled replacements, Lawrence
  Waterhouse has been selected to serve as Interim Fire Chief, while the City
  concludes  recruitment for a permanent replacement.  In order to be compliant
  with the 2013 Pension Reform Act, it is necessary for the City Council to take
  an action affirming the execution of such employment arrangements. The
  resolution  and agreement  satisfies  that requirement.

  Mayor Hepburn  called for public comment.

  One individual  spoke via the webinar.

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  The City Council thanked Chief Segura for his service and wished him well.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Crosby and unanimously carried by roll
  call to approve Resolution No, 21- 23, to execute an agreement with Lawrence
  Waterhouse  to provide  temporary, part- time employment.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 3, 2021, Page 4

9.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  Three individuals were called.

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

10.  Council Comments  Mayor Pro Tem Davis thanked Interim Finance Director Segura for his service
  to the City.

  Council Member Crosby reported that the County of Los Angeles is moving
  into the Yellow Tier and that vaccinations are moving along, which is all good
  news. He stated he look forward to meeting again as Council, but that it would
  have to be done safety.

  Council Member Carder stated she was elated that the County is moving into
  the Yellow Tier. She stated that she too, looked forward to meeting in person
  with the City Council, but that it would have to wait until the County gives the
  green light and that iYs safe. She reported that the Gold Line Construction is
  moving along. She reported that Tri- City Mental Health thanked and praised
  the La Verne Police for the awesome job working with them in dealing with the
  homeless. She gave a huge Thank You to all the City Employees who
  reported to work every day for the past fourteen ( 14) months during the
  pandemic. She stated that the residents should be appreciative that City
  services like public safety, streets, parks and water service, did not suffer
  during the pandemic.

  Council Member Lau reported that she and Council Member Davis were in a
  meeting with the Bonita Democrats and cities of Claremont and San Dimas
  were in attended to discuss cultural awareness. She reported that the
  University of La Verne is hosting an event in standing in solidarity with the
  Asian- Americans and Pacific Islanders against racist anti- Asian violence. She
  also thanked Chief Segura for his service. She too, looked forward to Council
  meeting again, but it has to be done safety. She thanked all City employees
  for their service during this unprecedented time.

  Mayor Hepburn also thanked City Departments for doing an outstanding job
  during the COVID- 19 pandemic and especially assisting the businesses in Old
  Town La Verne by closing D Street. He reported on the Old Town La Verne
  Business Improvement District meeting and their discussion on D Street
  closure. He reported that Bonita Unified School would be holding in- class
  school  starting  May 10, 2021.  He stated that June 15, 2021, is the target date
  for reopening, but that it would have to be done safety. He also thanked
  Interim  Fire Chief  Segura  for his  service to  the  City.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 3, 2021, Page 5

12.  Adjournment at 7: 50 p. m., in memory of Jefferson Hill Sr, a long- time La Verne resident who passed away on
  Friday, April 16, 2021. Mr. Hill was born on May 19, 1935, in Lake City, Tennessee. In 2003, Mr. Hill established
  the La Verne/San Dimas Meals on Wheels Program when he saw an unmet need for this service in both cities.
  The program started with seven recipients, and today serves over 50 meals daily. He served in the Air Force for
  finrenty- finro( 22) years as a Senior Master Sergeant during both the Korean and Vietnam Wars. He was a lifetime
  member of the VFW and is a past post-commander. He was instrumental in the campaign to construct the La
  Verne Veterans Memorial. In 2015, he was recognized by Assembly Member Holden for his years of services to
  his Country senring in the Air Force and the community. He was named Veteran of the Year for the 41 st
  Assembly District. He worked for Northrop as an aerospace engineer, earned a Masters in Psychology and went
  on to teach at several colleges. In 2015, he received the 50th Annual Older American Recognition Day Award.
  For his service to the community and commitment to the Veterans, he was honored as a Community Hero at the
  Los Angeles County Fair in 2015. His biggest passion was helping his fellow Veterans. He is survived by his wife
  Helen, his sons Jefferson Jr, Charles and daughter Evelyn.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, CMC
